title: PS5 GPU Equivalent: PC Graphics Card Match for Every Console
h1: PS5 GPU Equivalent (and Every Other Console)
description: The PS5 GPU is roughly an RX 6700, the PS5 Pro an RX 7700 XT, the Xbox Series X an RTX 2080 and the Steam Deck a GTX 1050. Every console and handheld charted.
dek: One chart for every console and handheld: the closest AMD, NVIDIA and Intel Arc card, the cheapest new card that matches it, and the catches that make console-to-PC matches rough.
quickAnswer: The PS5's GPU roughly equals a desktop RX 6700 or RTX 2070 Super, and a current Arc B580 or RTX 5060 matches it. The PS5 Pro lands near an RTX 4060 Ti to RTX 4070, the Xbox Series X near an RTX 2080, the Series S near a GTX 1650 Super, the Switch 2 near a GTX 1650 docked, and the Steam Deck near a GTX 1050.
intro: This chart matches every current console and PC handheld to the desktop graphics cards that perform most like it: PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X and Series S, Valve's Steam Machine, the last-generation PS4, PS4 Pro, Xbox One and One X, older consoles back to the PS3 and Xbox 360, the Steam Deck, the Z1 and Z2 Extreme handhelds (ROG Ally, Ally X, ROG Xbox Ally X, Legion Go) and the Nintendo Switch 2.

Console-to-PC matches are rougher than card-to-card ones. Consoles share one pool of memory between CPU and GPU, run games tuned for one fixed piece of hardware, and often render below their output resolution. The equivalents here follow the broad pattern of independent testing, including side-by-side comparisons of the same games on PC and console, rounded to the nearest card. We have not bench-tested these systems.

sections.h: How to Read This Chart, and Why Consoles Are Hard to Match
body: Each row lists the desktop card with the closest raster performance in games that run on both platforms. Roughly means within about 10 percent on average, a wider band than our [AMD vs NVIDIA chart](/amd-vs-nvidia-gpu-equivalents/), because console results depend so much on how well each game is optimized.

Three things shift the match. First, optimization: developers tune console versions for one GPU, so a well-made console port can beat a PC card that is a bit faster on paper. Second, memory: the PS5 and Xbox Series X have 16 GB of shared GDDR6, and games can use roughly 12 to 13.5 GB of it, more than an 8 GB graphics card holds. Third, settings: consoles often use dynamic resolution and settings below PC's high preset, so a PC at true 1440p high is doing more work.

Ray tracing is the weak spot of every AMD-based console. Their RDNA 2 graphics have the same limited ray-tracing hardware as the RX 6000 series, so with RT on they fall closer to an RTX 2060 class card. The PS5 Pro improved this, but not to NVIDIA's level.

sections.h: What Is the PS5 GPU Equivalent?
body: The PS5's GPU is closest to a desktop Radeon RX 6700 (the 10 GB card, not the XT). Both use RDNA 2 with 36 compute units; the PS5 runs them at up to 2.23 GHz for about 10.3 TFLOPS. In side-by-side game tests, the PS5 generally performs like an RTX 2070 Super, sometimes reaching RTX 2080 level in a well-optimized port.

In today's lineup, an [RTX 4060](/gear/rtx-4060/) or [Arc B580](/gear/arc-b580/) roughly matches or slightly beats a PS5 in raster, and the [RTX 5060](/gear/rtx-5060/) is a little faster again. All three add DLSS or XeSS, which usually look better than the PS5's upscaling. The [RX 6600](/gear/rx-6600/) is somewhat slower than a PS5. With ray tracing on, the PS5 falls closer to an RTX 2060 Super or RTX 3060.

Memory is the catch: PS5 ports built for its 16 GB pool often want more than 8 GB of video memory, so a 12 GB or 16 GB card such as the Arc B580 or [RX 9060 XT 16GB](/gear/rx-9060-xt-16gb/) matches the PS5 experience more reliably. Specs, clock speeds and the full breakdown are in [What GPU does the PS5 have?](/ps5-gpu-equivalent/)

sections.h: What Is the PS5 Pro GPU Equivalent?
body: Sony says the PS5 Pro renders about 45 percent faster than the PS5, using 60 compute units with faster memory. By that figure and independent testing, it lands roughly between an RTX 4060 Ti and an RTX 4070 in raster, close to an RX 7700 XT. Ray tracing improved more than raster, by Sony's figures two to three times the PS5's speed in some cases, though NVIDIA cards of the same raster tier still lead with heavy RT.

The Pro also adds PSSR, Sony's machine-learning upscaler, which plays a similar role to DLSS or FSR 4. On PC, an [RX 9060 XT 16GB](/gear/rx-9060-xt-16gb/) or [RTX 5060 Ti 16GB](/gear/rtx-5060-ti-16gb/) is the price-sensible way to get PS5 Pro class performance, and an [RTX 5070](/gear/rtx-5070/) clearly beats it. The full breakdown, CPU included, is in [PS5 Pro GPU equivalent](/ps5-pro-gpu-equivalent/).

sections.h: What Is the Xbox Series X GPU Equivalent?
body: The Xbox Series X GPU has 52 RDNA 2 compute units at 1.825 GHz, about 12.1 TFLOPS. On paper that sits between a desktop RX 6700 and RX 6700 XT. In game tests it performs roughly like an RTX 2080, a little ahead of the PS5 in many titles, though the PS5's higher clock speed lets it match or win in some.

In current cards, an RTX 4060 is close but slightly behind in raster, the Arc B580 is roughly even, and the RTX 5060 and [RX 6700 XT](/gear/rx-6700-xt/) are a little faster. The Series X gives games about 10 GB of fast memory for graphics, so the same 8 GB caution applies. More detail on both Xbox models: [Xbox Series X GPU equivalent](/xbox-series-x-gpu-equivalent/).

sections.h: What Is the Xbox Series S GPU Equivalent?
body: The Xbox Series S has 20 RDNA 2 compute units at 1.565 GHz, about 4 TFLOPS, and 10 GB of memory in total. In practice it performs roughly like a GTX 1650 Super or RX 6500 XT, and a little better than an Arc A380. Most games target 1080p or below on it, often with lower settings than the Series X.
Any current graphics card from the RTX 4060 or RX 7600 up is far faster than a Series S.

sections.h: What Is the Steam Machine GPU Equivalent?
body: Valve's Steam Machine uses a semi-custom AMD RDNA 3 GPU with 28 compute units and 8 GB of GDDR6, running at up to 2.45 GHz within a 110 W budget. On those specs it lands roughly at an RX 6600 XT or RTX 3060 12GB, about 15 to 20 percent below a desktop RX 7600, which has 32 compute units, higher clocks and more power. That puts it a step below a PS5's GPU in raster, though with a newer architecture and a much faster CPU.

These are estimates from the published specs; treat them as a range rather than a single card. The full breakdown, including the semi-custom Zen 4 6-core CPU, is in [Steam Machine GPU equivalent](/steam-machine-gpu-equivalent/).

sections.h: What Is the PS4 GPU Equivalent?
body: The PS4's GPU has 18 GCN compute units, about 1.84 TFLOPS, and performs roughly like a Radeon R7 265 or a GeForce GTX 750 Ti to GTX 1050. The PS4 Pro doubles the compute units to 36 at 4.2 TFLOPS, roughly an RX 470 or GTX 1060 3GB. The Xbox One X, at 6 TFLOPS, is the fastest of the generation and lands near an RX 580 or GTX 1060 6GB; the original Xbox One and One S sit near a GTX 750.

Every current graphics card is far faster than all of them. Even the cheapest current cards, such as an [RX 6600](/gear/rx-6600/), are several times a PS4, and a modern integrated GPU like the Radeon 780M is in the same range as a PS4 Pro. For the GTX 1060 and RX 580 class in today's terms, see [old GeForce equivalents](/old-nvidia-gpu-equivalents/) and [old Radeon equivalents](/old-amd-gpu-equivalents/).

sections.h: Older Console GPU Equivalents: PS3, Xbox 360 and the Original Switch
body: These consoles predate modern GPU features, so the match is to cards that are no longer sold. Any current integrated GPU, such as the Radeon Vega 8 in a Ryzen 5 5600G, is faster than all three; see our [integrated graphics equivalents](/integrated-graphics-equivalents/) chart for those matches.

The original Nintendo Switch's Tegra X1 has 256 NVIDIA Maxwell cores at 768 MHz docked and as low as 307 MHz handheld. Docked, that is roughly GT 730 (GDDR5) class, well below a GT 1030. The Switch 2 is a large step up, covered below.

sections.h: What Is the Steam Deck GPU Equivalent?
body: The Steam Deck's GPU has 8 RDNA 2 compute units at 1.0 to 1.6 GHz, about 1.6 TFLOPS, sharing 16 GB of LPDDR5 with a 4-core Zen 2 CPU. In games it performs roughly like a GTX 1050 or Arc A310, well below a GTX 1650, which suits its 1280 x 800 screen. The OLED model uses a die-shrunk version of the same chip, so performance is about the same. The LCD and OLED models are compared in [Steam Deck GPU equivalent](/steam-deck-gpu-equivalent/).

The Z1 Extreme handhelds (ASUS ROG Ally and Ally X, Lenovo Legion Go) use 12 RDNA 3 compute units, the same graphics as the Radeon 780M laptop chip. At their higher power settings they perform roughly like a GTX 1650, or about 1.5 to 2 times a Steam Deck in many games; at 15 W they fall much closer to the Deck. The Ally X adds faster memory, which helps a little.

sections.h: What Is the Z1 Extreme and Z2 Extreme GPU Equivalent?
body: The Ryzen Z1 Extreme in the ROG Ally, Ally X and Legion Go has 12 RDNA 3 compute units, the same graphics as the [Radeon 780M](/integrated-graphics-equivalents/). At 25 to 30 W it performs roughly like a GTX 1650; at 15 W it drops toward a GTX 1050 Ti, close to a Steam Deck.

The Ryzen Z2 Extreme in the ROG Xbox Ally X has 16 RDNA 3.5 compute units, the same class of graphics as the Radeon 890M, plus 8 Zen 5 cores. Expect GTX 1650 class performance at its higher power settings, ahead of the Z1 Extreme by a modest margin rather than a full tier. As with every handheld, the power mode you pick changes the match more than the chip does.

sections.h: What Is the Nintendo Switch 2 GPU Equivalent?
body: Nintendo has published less detail than Sony or Microsoft. What is widely reported is that the Switch 2 uses a custom NVIDIA chip with an Ampere-generation GPU of 1,536 CUDA cores, 12 GB of LPDDR5X and support for DLSS and hardware ray tracing. Clock speeds reported by developers and testers put it at roughly 3 TFLOPS docked and under 2 TFLOPS in handheld mode.

On those figures, its raw throughput docked is roughly GTX 1050 Ti to GTX 1650 class, a clear step above the Steam Deck but well below a PS5. DLSS lets games render at a lower resolution and look sharper than that suggests. Treat this match as an estimate; games built for the Switch 2 are tuned to it in ways a desktop card comparison cannot capture.

sections.h: What Is the PS5 and Xbox Series X CPU Equivalent?
body: The PS5 CPU is an 8-core, 16-thread AMD Zen 2 chip at up to 3.5 GHz, with a smaller cache than desktop Zen 2. It performs roughly like a Ryzen 7 3700X held to lower clocks, or a Ryzen 7 4700G; in games it lands closer to a Ryzen 5 3600. The Xbox Series X uses the same design at up to 3.8 GHz, slightly faster; the Series S runs at 3.6 GHz.

The PS5 Pro keeps the same 8-core Zen 2 design at a slightly higher clock, up to 3.85 GHz, so its CPU equivalent is the same: closer to a Ryzen 5 3600 in games. In Intel terms, both consoles land roughly at a Core i5-10400F to Core i7-10700 level in games.

Any current desktop CPU is much faster. A [Ryzen 5 7600](/gear/ryzen-5-7600/) or [Ryzen 7 5700X3D](/gear/ryzen-7-5700x3d/) comfortably beats a PS5 CPU, which matters in games that run at 30 or 60 fps on console because of the CPU, not the GPU. If your PC still has a Ryzen 5 2600 or 3600, it is roughly at console level; our [GPU guide for the Ryzen 5 2600 and 3600](/best-gpu-for-ryzen-5-2600-and-3600/) covers what to pair with it.

sections.h: What Is the Steam Deck CPU Equivalent?
body: The Steam Deck CPU is a 4-core, 8-thread AMD Zen 2 design at 2.4 to 3.5 GHz, sharing a 4 to 15 W power budget with the GPU. It performs roughly like a low-power laptop Ryzen 5 3500U or Ryzen 3 5300U, and below a desktop Ryzen 3 3100. In Intel terms it lands near a laptop Core i5-8250U to i5-10210U.

The Z1 Extreme handhelds have 8 Zen 4 cores and are much faster in CPU-heavy games, roughly a laptop Ryzen 7 7840U. The Steam Machine moves to 6 Zen 4 cores at a much higher power limit, well ahead of both.

sections.h: What PC Matches a PS5, PS5 Pro or Xbox Series X?
body: A PC that matches or slightly beats a PS5 in most games needs three things: a GPU at RTX 4060 level or better, a 6-core CPU from the last few years, and 16 GB of system RAM. For new parts, that means an [RTX 5060](/gear/rtx-5060/) or [Arc B580](/gear/arc-b580/) with a [Ryzen 5 7600](/gear/ryzen-5-7600/). For PS5 ports with heavy textures, the 12 GB B580 or a 16 GB [RX 9060 XT](/gear/rx-9060-xt-16gb/) is the safer choice. See [RTX 5060 vs Arc B580](/compare/rtx-5060-vs-arc-b580/) for that trade-off.

To match a PS5 Pro, step up to an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB or RX 9060 XT 16GB; to clearly beat it, an [RTX 5070](/gear/rtx-5070/) or [RX 9070](/gear/rx-9070/). On a tighter budget, an [RX 6600](/gear/rx-6600/) gets you most of the way to a PS5 at 1080p. Our [best budget graphics cards](/best-budget-graphics-card/) list ranks the options by price, and the [bottleneck calculator](/tools/bottleneck-calculator/) checks your CPU and GPU pairing.

mistakes: TFLOPS figures do not compare across architectures. The Z1 Extreme lists 8.6 TFLOPS, almost the Series X's number, because RDNA 3 counts dual-issue math; in games it is several times slower. Use measured game performance, not the spec-sheet number.
Buying an 8 GB card to match a PS5
A PS5 game can use roughly 12 GB or more for graphics. An 8 GB card with the same raw speed can stutter or need lower textures in PS5 ports. Choose 12 GB or 16 GB if console ports are what you play.
Expecting console settings to equal PC high
Consoles often run dynamic resolution and settings between PC's medium and high presets. A PC at native 1440p high is doing more work than the console version you are comparing it with.
Many console games are capped at 30 or 60 fps by the Zen 2 CPU. A faster desktop CPU is a big part of why PC versions can run at 100 fps or more with the same class of graphics card.
bottomLine: The quick matches are: PS5 to an RX 6700 or RTX 2070 Super, with an RTX 4060, RTX 5060 or Arc B580 matching or beating it today; PS5 Pro to an RTX 4060 Ti to RTX 4070; Xbox Series X to an RTX 2080; Series S to a GTX 1650 Super; Steam Deck to a GTX 1050; and Z1 Extreme handhelds to a GTX 1650 at full power. Choose 12 GB or more of VRAM for PS5 ports, and expect any modern 6-core CPU to beat a console's.

faqs.q: What GPU is equivalent to a PS5?
faqs.a: The desktop RX 6700 is the closest, with the same RDNA 2 design and 36 compute units, and by performance the PS5 roughly matches an RTX 2070 Super. Among cards on sale today, a $250 Arc B580 or $300 RTX 5060 matches or slightly beats it, and the B580's 12 GB of VRAM suits PS5 ports better.

faqs.q: Which console has the most powerful GPU?
faqs.a: The PS5 Pro. Its 60-compute-unit GPU lands roughly between an RTX 4060 Ti and an RTX 4070, ahead of the Xbox Series X (about an RTX 2080) and the base PS5 (about an RTX 2070 Super). The Switch 2 and handhelds such as the Steam Deck and ROG Ally sit at GTX 1050 to GTX 1650 level.

faqs.q: What GPU is equivalent to the PS4?
faqs.a: Roughly a GTX 750 Ti to GTX 1050, or a Radeon R7 265, from its 18 GCN compute units at about 1.84 TFLOPS. The PS4 Pro is near a GTX 1060 3GB or RX 470, and the Xbox One X near a GTX 1060 6GB or RX 580. Any current graphics card is far faster than all three.

faqs.q: What is the Xbox Series X GPU equivalent to?
faqs.a: Roughly an RTX 2080, and between a desktop RX 6700 and RX 6700 XT on paper. Today, an Arc B580 is about even with it, and an RTX 5060 or RX 6700 XT is a little faster.

faqs.q: What is the PS5 Pro GPU equivalent?
faqs.a: Roughly between an RTX 4060 Ti and an RTX 4070 in raster, close to an RX 7700 XT. Sony quotes about 45 percent faster rendering than the base PS5, with a bigger gain in ray tracing.

faqs.q: What GPU is the Steam Deck equal to?
faqs.a: Roughly a GTX 1050 or Arc A310. The Steam Deck's 8 RDNA 2 compute units make about 1.6 TFLOPS, which is enough for its 800p screen but well below a GTX 1650.

faqs.q: What GPU is equivalent to the Nintendo Switch 2?
faqs.a: Roughly a GTX 1050 Ti to GTX 1650 when docked. That is an estimate from its widely reported 1,536-core NVIDIA Ampere GPU at about 3 TFLOPS. It is a clear step above a Steam Deck and well below a PS5, and DLSS lets games look sharper than those numbers suggest.

faqs.q: What is the Steam Machine GPU equivalent?
faqs.a: On its published specs, a 28-compute-unit RDNA 3 GPU with 8 GB of GDDR6 at up to 2.45 GHz, the Steam Machine lands roughly at an RX 6600 XT or RTX 3060 12GB, about 15 to 20 percent below an RX 7600 and a step below a PS5. Treat it as an estimate from specs.
